$comment: Overlay of tab 1 (WI-004) on the vendored Package Overview schema: the fields, required flags, enums and formats come from the schema; this file adds only labels, help, notes, the 'Why we ask (client)' lines and what the customer never sees. Changing a line here is a text change, not a spec change.

labels./thirdPartyInformationResources: Third-party information resources within the Minimum Assessment Scope

help./serviceIdentification/fedRampPackageId: Only if FedRAMP already assigned you one
help./serviceIdentification/ueiNumber: If no UEI is available leave this blank
help./serviceIdentification/logo: PNG or JPEG, at least 256 px wide, up to 2 MB. Ignyte hosts it for your FedRAMP listing.
help./contactInformation: Include at least one Security contact and one Sales contact.

notes./thirdPartyInformationResources: This is not limited to services that touch federal data.

why.$source: Brain projects/maaz20x/docs/maaz20x-intake-questionnaire.md §2, column 'Why we ask (client)', questions 1 to 5 (Christina Martinson, 2026-10-23).
/serviceIdentification/providerName: Your company's legal name appears in your FedRAMP listing and package. If you have a UEI from SAM.gov, it is part of your public FedRAMP information; if you don't have one, leave it blank. Your headquarters location is for your consultant's records.
/contactInformation: FedRAMP expects a senior official to accept any decision not to follow a rule, so we need to know who signs off for your company. (ex. CISO, CEO)
This is who we work with week to week on technical questions and evidence, so we know who to ask and who to keep informed.
/serviceIdentification/serviceName: FedRAMP lists your product and each service it covers using the names you use in your marketing, so agencies can see exactly what is and isn't covered.
/serviceProperties/serviceType: Your public FedRAMP information shows your service model and deployment model, and they help define what is in scope.
